key_insight: A finite element method with linearly implicit Euler time stepping achieves optimal strong error rates for semilinear SPDEs with additive noise, even when the initial data is nonsmooth.
engineering_relevance: This gives a reliable numerical framework for simulating stochastic diffusion-type systems where early-time singular behavior and low-regularity inputs matter.
method: Standard finite element spatial discretization of the semilinear parabolic SPDE
Linearly implicit Euler scheme for time integration
Regularity analysis that isolates initial-data singularity into an integrable temporal factor
evidence_signal: The abstract reports proven strong convergence rates of O(h^β) for the semidiscrete method and O(h^β + k^{β/2}) for the fully discrete scheme, supported by numerical experiments.
watch_item: The optimal rates are stated for positive times away from t = 0, so very early-time behavior may still require care in implementation and interpretation.
paper_title: Optimal Error Estimates of a Finite Element Method for Semilinear SPDEs with Additive Noise and Nonsmooth Initial Data
